note: Public scientific sanitizers over OpenMM's pure-Python API layer: wrappers/python/openmm/unit/ (the typed dimensional-analysis system: Quantity/Unit conversion, sqrt, dot/norm dimensional consistency, physical-constant reference values), wrappers/python/openmm/app/internal/unitcell.py (periodic box vector <-> lengths/angles geometry), wrappers/python/openmm/app/element.py (element table lookups), wrappers/python/openmm/app/topology.py and forcefield.py (System/Topology consistency, mass conservation under hydrogen mass repartitioning, constrained-angle geometry), wrappers/python/openmm/app/modeller.py (topology merge count conservation), wrappers/python/openmm/vec3.py (coordinate primitive). Inactive unless SCIBENCH_TRIGGER_LOG is set. See openmm_pilot/README.md, openmm_pilot/LAW_CANDIDATES.md, and repo-root SANITIZER.md. OpenMM's compiled C++/CUDA/OpenCL numerical core (openmmapi/, platforms/) is NOT instrumented -- see README.md's instrumentation-location rationale. 19 sanitizers total (one drafted candidate, OM-PBC-004, was rejected and retired after its originally-formulated law was found false during Step 4 tolerance derivation; see LAW_CANDIDATES.md). One genuine OpenMM library defect was found during tolerance/precondition derivation (OM-ELEM-001: Element.getByMass can never return curium or lawrencium due to duplicate-mass dict-key collisions in element.py's built-in table) and drafted, not filed, as openmm_pilot/issues/ISSUE_1_getByMass_duplicate_mass_table_entries.md per SANITIZER.md 8.1.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: a physical quantity expressed in different, mutually compatible units
sanitizers.precondition: any Quantity with a well-defined unit, converted to any compatible unit and back
sanitizers.invariant: q.in_units_of(u2).in_units_of(u1) == q for any Quantity q and compatible unit u2
sanitizers.observation_point: inside in_units_of, after computing the result, re-converting back to the original unit and comparing
sanitizers.rationale: unit conversion is used throughout OpenMM's Python layer (structure I/O, system construction, energy reporting); a non-invertible conversion pair would silently corrupt any round-tripped quantity
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: 9-unit-pair x 6-magnitude-scale sweep (1e-8..1e12) on the unmodified pinned checkout found bit-level agreement (worst observed ratio 0.98x eps64, nanometer<->meter at 1e-3). Tolerance set to 100x*eps64*max(1,|value|) for headroom.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: conversion factor between two compatible physical units
sanitizers.precondition: any three mutually compatible units u1, u2, u3 (same physical dimension)
sanitizers.observation_point: inside conversion_factor_to, using an independent intermediate unit already present in the conversion's own base-unit decomposition
sanitizers.alarm: relative difference between the direct and via-intermediate factor exceeds 1e-9
sanitizers.rationale: conversion_factor_to is the single primitive every other unit operation is built on; non-associative composition would silently corrupt any quantity converted through a transitive chain
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: 4-group sweep (length/energy/time/pressure units) found bit-exact-to-near-exact transitivity (worst observed relative error ~1.3e-16). Tolerance set to 1e-9 for large headroom while remaining far tighter than 1.0.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: conversion factor between two compatible physical units
sanitizers.precondition: any two mutually compatible units u1, u2
sanitizers.observation_point: inside conversion_factor_to, computing the reverse factor and multiplying
sanitizers.alarm: product differs from 1.0 by more than 1e-9
sanitizers.rationale: isolates the simplest two-unit case of the same underlying primitive as OM-UNIT-002, catching a defect a three-unit chain might miss if the intermediate happens to coincide with an endpoint
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: pairwise sweep across 5 unit groups found bit-exact (0.0) product error for every pair tested. Tolerance set to 1e-9.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: square root of a dimensioned physical quantity
sanitizers.precondition: any positive scalar Quantity whose unit's base-dimension exponents are all even
sanitizers.invariant: squaring sqrt(q) via an independent operator path (Quantity.__mul__, not Unit.sqrt/conversion_factor_to again) reproduces q
sanitizers.observation_point: inside Quantity.sqrt, after computing the result, squaring it via __mul__ and comparing to the original value expressed in the squared unit
sanitizers.rationale: sqrt is used by Quantity.sqrt/unit_math.sqrt, which appear in norm/RMSD-style calculations (unitcell.py's computeLengthsAndAngles uses norm); an off-by-a-conversion-factor unit from sqrt would silently scale every quantity built from it
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: 6-scale sweep (1e-6..1e10) found zero deviation. Tolerance set to 100*eps64*sqrt(scale) for headroom.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: square root of a dimensioned physical quantity, via the free-function delegation path
sanitizers.precondition: any positive scalar Quantity whose unit's base-dimension exponents are all even
sanitizers.invariant: squaring unit_math.sqrt(q)'s value (an independent __mul__ re-derivation) must equal q's own value expressed in the squared result unit
sanitizers.observation_point: inside unit_math.sqrt, after the val.sqrt() delegation returns
sanitizers.rationale: two structurally different code paths (Quantity.sqrt method vs. the free unit_math.sqrt function) computing the same physical quantity must agree; drift would mean callers get different numeric answers depending on which spelling they used
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: same empirical sweep as OM-UNIT-004 (zero observed deviation). FIX (regression testing, wrappers/python/tests/TestUnits.py): the first implementation compared result**2 (correctly converted to the result's own unit) against the ORIGINAL quantity's raw ._value field without converting units -- false-fired on u.sqrt(1.0*kilogram*calorie) because 1.0 kg*cal genuinely differs numerically from its value in kg*joule (the calorie->joule factor, 4.184) despite being the same physical quantity; a checker-side unit-handling bug, not an OpenMM defect. Fixed by converting the original quantity into the squared result's unit via val.value_in_unit(result.unit**2) before comparing -- an independent code path from Quantity.sqrt's own internal arithmetic. Re-verified: sqrt(kilogram*calorie) and 3 other unit-mismatched cases now silent; isolated-sensitivity still fires; full 197-test regression suite (2 consecutive rounds) clean with zero triggers.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: Euclidean norm of a vector of dimensioned quantities
sanitizers.precondition: any 3-vector of compatible-unit Quantity components (e.g. Vec3-valued positions)
sanitizers.invariant: dot(x,x).unit is compatible with x[0].unit**2, and norm(x).unit is compatible with x[0].unit
sanitizers.observation_point: inside norm, after computing dot(x,x) and the sqrt call
sanitizers.alarm: either compatibility check fails (boolean structural check, no numerical tolerance)
sanitizers.rationale: norm/dot are used by unitcell.py's computeLengthsAndAngles to turn periodic box vectors into lengths and angles; a dimensional inconsistency would silently corrupt box geometry for arbitrary box-vector units

sanitizers.invariant: MOLAR_GAS_CONSTANT_R's SI value matches the CODATA 2018 / 2019-SI-exact reference value (8.31446261815324 J/(mol K))
sanitizers.observation_point: at module import, comparing against an independently-maintained CODATA reference constant in the checker module (not the adjacent NA*kB multiplication that defines R in this file, which would be a tautology)
sanitizers.alarm: relative difference from the CODATA reference exceeds 1e-9
sanitizers.rationale: R feeds every thermostat/barostat temperature-coupling calculation in the app layer; a transcribed-digit error in AVOGADRO_CONSTANT_NA or BOLTZMANN_CONSTANT_kB would silently bias every simulated temperature
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: R is exact post-2019 SI redefinition (both NA and kB are defined-exact); 1e-9 is a transcription-error check, not a rounding-tolerance check.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: the speed of light in vacuum
sanitizers.observation_point: at module import, exact-equality comparison against the SI-exact reference value
sanitizers.alarm: any deviation at all -- this constant is exact by definition (SI 1983), not measured
sanitizers.rationale: same pattern as OM-UNIT-007 (SANITIZER.md 5.7 physical-constant-reference pattern), a distinct and independently-defined constant not derived from other constants in this file
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: exact-equality check; no rounding tolerance applies.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: periodic simulation box geometry, as lengths+angles vs. box-vector representations
sanitizers.precondition: lengths/angles whose corresponding pre-reduction vector triple already satisfies OpenMM's reduced-form round() tests (round(b_x/a_x)==0, round(c_y/b_y)==0, round(c_x/a_x)==0) -- NARROWED during Step 4 tolerance derivation; see fix note below
sanitizers.invariant: computeLengthsAndAngles(computePeriodicBoxVectors(a,b,c,alpha,beta,gamma)) reproduces (a,b,c,alpha,beta,gamma), for inputs satisfying the corrected precondition
sanitizers.observation_point: inside computePeriodicBoxVectors, after computing and reducing (a,b,c), calling computeLengthsAndAngles on the result and comparing to the original inputs, gated on the precondition check
sanitizers.alarm: any of the six reconstructed values differs from the input by more than 100*eps64*length_scale (lengths) or 100*eps64 (angles)
sanitizers.rationale: this pair of functions is OpenMM's own author-provided cross-check between two independent geometric descriptions of a simulation box (PDB CRYST1 records, Amber/Gromacs box specs); within its valid precondition, a reduction bug that changed cell shape would silently corrupt every downstream PBC calculation
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: FIX (pre-instrumentation, Step 4): the naive precondition 'any valid box shape' was falsified by a 20-case sweep -- a triclinic case with lengths/angles corresponding to an UNREDUCED vector triple showed a 0.4-radian round-trip discrepancy, traced to OpenMM's own intentional, documented reduced-form transform genuinely changing b's length and derived angles for far-from-90-degree inputs. Not a defect -- a checker-precondition gap. Precondition corrected to only pre-reduced inputs; re-swept 20 cases (cubic/orthorhombic/skewed/mild-triclinic x 5 length scales 0.5-5000nm) under the corrected precondition: bit-level agreement (worst ratio 1.0x eps64 angles, 0.8x eps64 lengths). Tolerance set to 100x for headroom.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: periodic simulation cell volume (determinant of the box-vector matrix)
sanitizers.precondition: any three linearly independent box vectors (a,b,c) forming a valid non-degenerate unit cell
sanitizers.invariant: det([a,b,c]) is unchanged by reducePeriodicBoxVectors -- integer lattice-vector reduction is a unimodular (det=1) shear and must preserve volume
sanitizers.observation_point: inside reducePeriodicBoxVectors, computing the determinant of the input triple before reduction and the output triple after
sanitizers.rationale: cell volume determines particle density, pressure calculations, and PME reciprocal-space grid spacing; a reduction step that silently changed volume would corrupt every physical quantity computed from box geometry after reduction
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: same mathematical structure as pymatgen's PM-LAT-003 (LLL reduction volume invariance). Tolerance follows the same T-discipline pattern: 100*eps64*cond*scale^3, simplified here to 100*eps64*scale^3 since the reduction shear is well-conditioned by construction (unimodular integer combinations).

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: the 'reduced form' contract for periodic box vectors
sanitizers.precondition: any valid (non-degenerate) box-vector triple passed through reducePeriodicBoxVectors
sanitizers.invariant: the output of reducePeriodicBoxVectors must satisfy exactly the reduced-form inequalities Topology.setPeriodicBoxVectors itself enforces by raising ValueError
sanitizers.observation_point: inside reducePeriodicBoxVectors, after computing the reduced triple, evaluating setPeriodicBoxVectors's own inequality predicates against it without calling setPeriodicBoxVectors (to avoid a re-entrant production call)
sanitizers.alarm: any reduced-form inequality is violated (with rounding slack for boundary cases)
sanitizers.rationale: setPeriodicBoxVectors is the API contract every downstream OpenMM component relies on for 'this box is in reduced form'; if reducePeriodicBoxVectors's arithmetic and setPeriodicBoxVectors's validation ever disagreed, code that reduces a box and hands it to setPeriodicBoxVectors (a documented common pattern) would raise on input its own reduction function just produced
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: boundary slack of 1e-9*max(1,scale) matches the rounding-noise floor used elsewhere in this file's reduction arithmetic; structural inequality check, not a magnitude-scaled numerical comparison.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: the chemical element whose tabulated atomic mass is closest to a query mass
sanitizers.precondition: any mass value within the span of masses in the element table
sanitizers.invariant: the element returned by getByMass must have the minimum |tabulated_mass - query| among all elements in the table (documented: 'Get the element whose mass is CLOSEST to the requested mass')
sanitizers.observation_point: inside getByMass, after the early-bailout optimized loop determines best_guess, before returning -- compared against an independent brute-force linear scan over the full element table
sanitizers.alarm: the brute-force closest element differs from best_guess
sanitizers.rationale: getByMass uses an early-bailout optimization over a table sorted by mass; a bailout or comparison-direction error would silently return the wrong element for masses near a table boundary, which downstream code (element inference from mass values) would use as ground truth without further validation
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: exact-match structural check (element identity), no numerical tolerance. FINDING: a 116-boundary brute-force sweep (every adjacent tabulated-mass midpoint, +/-1e-6 dalton offsets to break exact ties) found 8 genuine non-tie mismatches, root-caused to two duplicate-mass pairs in the table (berkelium/curium both 247 Da; dubnium/lawrencium both 262 Da) silently colliding in the _elements_by_mass dict cache, permanently hiding curium and lawrencium from getByMass. Confirmed as a genuine OpenMM defect (not a checker artifact) by reading source and reproducing directly. No existing upstream report found after searching openmm/openmm issues. Drafted (not filed) as issues/ISSUE_1_getByMass_duplicate_mass_table_entries.md per SANITIZER.md 8.1.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: the canonical element for an atomic number shared by multiple isotopes (e.g. hydrogen/deuterium)
sanitizers.precondition: constructing two or more Element instances that share the same atomic number
sanitizers.invariant: getByAtomicNumber(n) must return the element with the minimum mass among all elements sharing atomic number n (stated explicitly in source: 'we want to choose the lighter one ... since it's the canonical element')
sanitizers.observation_point: inside Element.__init__'s collision-resolution branch, after the conditional update, verified against an independent scan of all registered elements sharing the same atomic number
sanitizers.alarm: getByAtomicNumber(n).mass is not the minimum mass among same-atomic-number elements
sanitizers.rationale: getByAtomicNumber is used wherever code needs 'the' element for an atomic number (e.g. mapping PDB/CIF atomic numbers to element identity); an inverted comparison would silently make deuterium the canonical 'hydrogen' for every atomic-number-based lookup
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: exact structural check (minimum-mass identity); no numerical tolerance. Verified silent on the unmodified table (hydrogen correctly canonical over deuterium).

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: orthorhombic periodic box dimensions, as two officially-documented alternative representations
sanitizers.precondition: any three positive lengths (a valid orthorhombic/rectangular box), observed via getUnitCellDimensions only when the most recent box-vector-setting call on this Topology instance was setUnitCellDimensions itself (not an intervening setPeriodicBoxVectors call)
sanitizers.observation_point: inside getUnitCellDimensions, comparing the diagonal it extracts against a checker-only side-channel value recorded by setUnitCellDimensions (never read by production code, so this is not a re-read of the same _periodicBoxVectors attribute -- avoids the SANITIZER.md 5.2 tautology of comparing getUnitCellDimensions against itself)
sanitizers.rationale: getUnitCellDimensions is documented as 'an alternative to setPeriodicBoxVectors() for the case of a rectangular box'; if the two accessors' Vec3-index conventions ever drifted apart, every consumer of the simple-rectangular-box API would silently get axes swapped or scaled wrong
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: same length-scaled eps64 tolerance derivation as OM-PBC-001 (bit-level agreement observed for straightforward diagonal read/write, no rounding path involved). FIX (regression testing, wrappers/python/tests/TestForceField.py): the checker-only side channel was not invalidated when setPeriodicBoxVectors (a distinct method) later changed _periodicBoxVectors on the same Topology instance -- false-fired in test_PeriodicBoxVectors, whose setUp() calls setUnitCellDimensions(2,2,2) and later calls setPeriodicBoxVectors(different_vectors) on self.pdb1.topology without ever calling setUnitCellDimensions again; getUnitCellDimensions then compared the new (correct) box against the stale (2,2,2) recording. A checker-side bug (missing side-channel invalidation), not an OpenMM defect. Fixed by deleting the side-channel attribute inside setPeriodicBoxVectors whenever it runs. Re-verified: the exact reproduction (set dims, then setPeriodicBoxVectors, then getUnitCellDimensions) is now silent; a synthetic stale-side-channel injection still fires (proving the checker did not just go silent); full 197-test regression suite (2 consecutive rounds) clean with zero triggers.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: particle count and ordering correspondence between a System and its source Topology
sanitizers.precondition: any Topology that createSystem successfully matches against templates (no exception raised)
sanitizers.invariant: createSystem(topology).getNumParticles() == topology.getNumAtoms(), with particles in the same order as atoms (createSystem's own documented contract)
sanitizers.observation_point: at the end of createSystem, immediately before returning the System
sanitizers.rationale: this ordering/count contract is load-bearing for every caller that indexes into System particles using Topology atom indices (the standard OpenMM usage pattern, e.g. applying position restraints by atom index); a silent particle-count drift would misalign every subsequent by-index operation without error
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: exact-equality structural check (particle count is an integer); no numerical tolerance.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: total mass of a molecular System under hydrogen-mass repartitioning
sanitizers.precondition: createSystem called with a non-None hydrogenMass on any topology with at least one hydrogen bonded to a heavy atom
sanitizers.invariant: total system mass (sum over all particles) after hydrogenMass repartitioning equals the total mass before repartitioning (createSystem's documented promise: 'Any mass added to a hydrogen is subtracted from the heavy atom to keep their total mass the same')
sanitizers.observation_point: at the end of the hydrogenMass adjustment block, comparing an independent running total accumulated during the original atom-adding loop (before any repartitioning) against sys.getParticleMass summed over all particles after repartitioning
sanitizers.alarm: relative difference in total mass exceeds 100*eps64*num_atoms*max(1,|total|)
sanitizers.rationale: hydrogen mass repartitioning is widely used to enable longer MD timesteps; a global mass-conservation violation (distinct from the per-pair arithmetic, which is tautologically conserving by construction -- see LAW_CANDIDATES.md's tautology-avoidance note) would silently drift the simulated system's total mass, density, and mass-weighted analyses
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: standard floating-point summation error bound scaled by particle count; not empirically swept (the check is a global-sum consistency check, not a magnitude-sensitive re-call comparison).

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: the coordinate primitive underlying every position, velocity, force, and box vector in the Python API
sanitizers.precondition: any Vec3 of finite floating-point components
sanitizers.invariant: -(-v) == v component-wise (exact under IEEE 754), and v + (-v) == (0,0,0) component-wise (exact under IEEE 754)
sanitizers.observation_point: inside __neg__, computing the double-negation and the sum-with-negation and comparing
sanitizers.alarm: any component differs -- exact equality, not a tolerance, since IEEE 754 negation and additive-inverse cancellation for finite floats are exact operations
sanitizers.rationale: Vec3 is the coordinate primitive used throughout the Python API, including unitcell.py's own reduction arithmetic; a sign or component-ordering bug in __neg__ would silently invert or scramble coordinates for every caller relying on unary negation
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: exact equality; IEEE 754 guarantees zero rounding error for negation and additive-inverse cancellation of finite floats.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: the constraint distance derived from a constrained bond angle via the law of cosines
sanitizers.precondition: any residue template where an angle is marked constrained and both of its constituent bonds have a determined length
sanitizers.invariant: the law-of-cosines-derived constraint length must equal the Euclidean distance obtained by an independent 3D-geometry construction (placing the three atoms at consistent positions from the same l1, l2, theta and measuring the straight-line distance directly)
sanitizers.observation_point: inside postprocessSystem's constrained-angle branch, immediately after computing length via the law of cosines
sanitizers.alarm: relative difference between the law-of-cosines length and the independently-constructed-geometry length exceeds 100*eps64*max(l1,l2)
sanitizers.rationale: this constraint length is what SETTLE/rigid-body machinery in the C++ core enforces at every timestep for constrained angles (e.g. rigid water's H-O-H angle, or heavy-atom angle constraints under HAngles); an error would silently constrain every affected angle to the wrong physical geometry for the entire simulation
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: 6-case sweep (bond lengths 1e-4..1.0, angles 10-179 degrees) found worst observed ratio ~3.2x eps64. Tolerance set to 100x for headroom.

sanitizers.scientific_quantity: atom, bond, residue, and chain counts when merging two molecular topologies
sanitizers.precondition: any two Topology/positions pairs with consistent atom-count-to-position-count correspondence (add's documented input contract)
sanitizers.invariant: after self.add(addTopology, addPositions), the merged topology's atom/bond/residue/chain counts equal the sum of the two inputs' respective counts
sanitizers.observation_point: at the end of add, comparing the final topology's own count methods against counts computed before the merge (self.topology.getNum*() + addTopology.getNum*(), recorded before either topology is copied)
sanitizers.alarm: any of the four counts does not equal the corresponding sum
sanitizers.rationale: Modeller.add is the standard way to combine a solute and a solvent box or merge molecular components before simulation; a silent atom-count drift would build a System with the wrong composition without error, corrupting every downstream physical quantity (total charge, total mass, particle count)
sanitizers.tolerance_derivation: exact-equality structural check (all four quantities are integers); no numerical tolerance.
